prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map depicts an outdoor scene next to a house wall on the right (0.4–1.5 m away, receding into the background in frame 4 up to ~3 m) and an open yard with bare trees and sky on the left and above (>10 m away, rendered black). In frames 1–3 and 5, a standing man wearing glasses and a beanie is roughly 0.7–1.0 m in front of the camera wearer, while a baby held in his right arm (to the left in the frame, below his shoulder) is slightly nearer at about 0.5–0.8 m and zero distance from the man; both are within arm's reach of the camera wearer and of each other, with their lower bodies cropped below the bottom edge of the frame. The man faces toward the camera wearer in frames 1, 3, and 5 and angles his head slightly right in frame 2 while the baby faces away toward the man, and in frame 4 the camera wearer turns sharply rightward toward the house exterior (showing windows, a bird feeder pole at ~2 m, and an electric meter), moving the man and baby completely out of view before turning back in frame 5 as they approach slightly closer (~0.5–0.8 m). Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the foreground baby and house wall corner from the mid-ground man and distant tree branches, and even captures thin overhead string lights and the bird feeder pole in frames 2–5. However, the depth map is unreliable on reflective window glass (which blends smoothly with the surrounding wall depth) and blurs the depth boundary where the baby's head overlaps the man's shoulder in frame 5.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates the foreground people against a black background across the five frames, locating the standing man (~0.7–1.0 m from the camera wearer) at center-right and the held baby (~0.5–0.8 m away, directly in front of and touching the man's right side) at lower-left within arm's reach of both the man and the camera wearer. In frames 1–3, the man's upper body and head (facing the camera wearer in frames 1 and 3, turned slightly right in frame 2) are segmented as a pink 'person' mask and the baby (facing away/inward, with lower body occluded and cropped at the bottom edge) as a brown 'person' mask that partially occludes the man's right arm and torso. In frame 4, as the camera wearer turns right toward the house wall (~0.5–3 m away), no masks appear because both individuals leave the field of view, and when the camera turns back in frame 5 with the pair slightly closer (~0.5–0.8 m), both reappear lower in the frame as the man looks toward the camera wearer. This map makes the distinct instance boundary between the baby's silhouette and the man's chest in frames 1–3 immediately clear despite overlapping clothing and shadows in the RGB image. However, it is unreliable for scene layout and objects—omitting the house, windows, trees, and string lights entirely—and in frame 5 it completely misses the baby's head, splits the man's torso into two separate 'person' masks (pink on the left, cyan on the right), and hallucinates a tiny false 'person' mask at the bottom-right corner on the window frame.
descriptions.pose: The skeleton map tracks upper-body and hand keypoints on a black background for the standing man (~0.7–1.0 m in front of the camera wearer, within arm's reach) while omitting the house wall to the right and trees above and to the left. In frame 1, facial keypoints show the man facing and looking toward the camera wearer, yellow shoulder-to-wrist lines show both arms extending downward, and a dense magenta hand skeleton locates his raised left hand near the lower-right edge (~0.6 m away) while his right arm holds the baby on the left (~0.5–0.8 m away, within his arm's reach). Across frames 2 and 3, his head keypoints shift downward in the frame and turn slightly right in frame 2 before facing the camera wearer again in frame 3, while his left forearm drops out of view below the bottom edge and his right forearm/wrist keypoints appear angled upward in frame 3 where he supports the baby; in frame 4 all keypoints vanish as the camera wearer turns right toward the house, and in frame 5 the man's tilted shoulder line and facial keypoints return lower in the frame as he stands closer (~0.6–0.8 m). Compared to RGB, the pose map explicitly reveals the articulated joint angles of the man's shoulders, elbows, and left fingers in frame 1 and the hidden orientation of his right forearm supporting the baby in frame 3. However, the map is unreliable because it fails to detect any body or hand keypoints for the baby across all frames, misses the man's hands in frames 2–3 where they are occluded or cropped at the frame boundary, and falsely projects a magenta hand skeleton directly onto the man's face and glasses in frame 5.
